name: Facet
text:
**Decision:** Make the graph’s nodes pulse gently when idle—no hover, no click—just a slow, rhythmic glow. This keeps the interface alive without distracting from the data.

**Why:** A static graph dies on screen; a pulsing one signals "fresh data" without shouting. It’s subtle enough for focus but obvious enough to feel dynamic.

**Trade-off:** Some users might find it distracting at first, but the liveliness outweighs the friction—it’s a habit users adapt to in seconds, not minutes.

name: Pane
text: The pulse risks lulling users into ignoring it—like a ticking clock they tune out—while still failing to guide their eyes to what matters. A better signal is adaptive contrast: darken the graph’s edges when idle, brighten them when data changes, so users see *where* to look without motion noise. Settle it with a quick A/B test: measure time-to-first-glance at new data with both designs.
